units: Erub. 101ᵃ, v. אַלְמָנָה.—נעל ד׳ בפני לוין to shut the door to borrowers, to render credit difficult.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80b:10">B. Kam. 80ᵇ</cite> <he>ד׳ הננעלת וכ׳</he> a door once shut is not easily opened, i.e. it requires ardent prayer to regain divine grace after a calamity has set in; a. fr.—
Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. VI, 7 של ד׳ on hinges, v. מַסְחֵיט.—Pl. דְּלָתוֹת, constr. דַּלְתוֹת.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 14:4">Lev. R. s. 14</cite> <he>יש ד׳ וכ׳</he> a woman’s womb has doors (muscles, ref. to <cite ref="Job 3:10">Job III, 10</cite>); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Parah 3:2">Par. III, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Parah 3:2">Tosef. ib. III</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Parah 2:2">II</cite>), 2 <he>על גביהן ד׳</he> a seat of boards on hinges upon the backs of the oxen; <cite ref="Sukkah 21a:7">Succ. 21ᵃ</cite>.—

<cite ref="Yoma 9b:15">Yoma 9ᵇ</cite> <he>כד׳</he> vacillating like doors, v. <cite ref="D00824"><he>דַּלּוּת</he></cite>. [<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:2:31">Y. Kidd. I, 59ᵈ</cite> top, v. <cite ref="D00849"><he>דְּלַעַת</he></cite>.]
